related_questions.question: How long after I'm exposed to COVID will I get it?
related_questions.snippet: Key points. People with COVID-19 have a wide range of symptoms ranging from mild symptoms to severe illness. Symptoms may appear 2-14 days after exposure to the virus. Symptoms may start as mild, and some people will progress to more severe symptoms.
related_questions.title: Symptoms of COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: Can I go to work with COVID in Kentucky?
related_questions.snippet: Anyone who has tested positive for COVID-19 should notify their employer and self-isolate (stay away from work and others) for 10 days. If symptoms fully resolve, isolation may be shortened and end after day 5 on the first day without symptoms. If no symptoms, isolate for 5 days from the date of the test.
related_questions.title: COVID-19 in the Workplace

related_questions.question: What is Kentucky hardship relief?
related_questions.snippet: Utilizing Team Kentucky Funds, Community Action Kentucky will provide eligible applicants with financial vouchers of up to $1,000 per household. Vouchers may be used to help offset the following approved expenses: Rent, Mortgage, Food/Grocery and Utility Costs.
related_questions.title: Team Kentucky Fund - Tri-County Community Action Agency

related_questions.question: How many times will I get COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People can be reinfected with SARS-CoV-2 multiple times. Each time a person is infected with SARS-CoV-2, they have a risk of developing Long COVID. Long COVID symptoms and conditions can emerge, persist, resolve, and reemerge over weeks and months.
